summary.text: Son of Priam whom the old king chid among the nine sons at Hector's ransom and whom Apollodorus counts among the king's children by other women — distinct from Hippothous the Pelasgian captain (`hippothous-pelasgian`) who dragged Patroclus until Ajax smote him.

story.text: When Priam prepared to ransom Hector, he called to nine sons — among them Hippothous beside Helenus, Paris, goodly Agathon, Pammon, Antiphonus, Polites, Deïphobus, and lordly Dius — and wished they had all fallen when mighty Hector died.
Apollodorus names Hippothous among the many sons Priam begot by other women.
